sentences.text: English podcast. My name is Emily. I am happy you are here today.
We will talk about Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan is a country with old cities,
mountains and strong traditions in Central Asia.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready? Let's begin.
Where is Uzbekistan?
Uzbekistan is in Central Asia.
It is next to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan and Turkmenistan.
It has no sea, but it has rivers, deserts and mountains.
What is the capital city of Uzbekistan?
The capital city is Tashkent.
Tashkent is a big and modern city.
It has parks, markets, mosques and museums.
Other important cities are Samarkand, famous for blue buildings in ancient history.
Bukhara, an old silk road city with many mosques,
Kiva, a beautiful walled city in the desert,
Andijan, a busy city in the east.
How many people live in Uzbekistan?
About 36 million people live in Uzbekistan.
It is the most populated country in Central Asia.
Many people live in cities, but also in villages and farms.
What language do people speak in Uzbekistan?
The official language is Uzbek.
Many people also speak Russian, especially in big cities.
Some people speak Tajik, Karakal Pak and English in schools.
What is the weather like in Uzbekistan?
Uzbekistan has a dry continental climate, hot summers, very dry and sunny.
Cold winters with some snow.
Spring and autumn, short and nice.
Rain is rare, especially in the desert areas.
What does Uzbekistan look like?
Uzbekistan has mountains in the east, deserts and plains in the west.
The Amudarya and Sirdarya rivers.
Beautiful historic cities with colorful buildings.
It was an important stop on the Silk Road long ago.
What animals live in Uzbekistan?
In Uzbekistan, you can see wolves, foxes and wild cats, horses, sheep and camels, birds like eagles, falcons and owls, lizards, snakes and insects in the desert.
Some animals live in mountains, others and plains or dry lands.
What do people eat in Uzbekistan?
Uzbek food is rich, warm and often made with rice and meat.
People eat bread, especially flat bread called non rice, noodles and dumplings.
Lamb, beef and chicken, carrots, onions and potatoes.
Popular dishes, plav, rice with meat, carrots and onions, national dish, lagmen, hand-pulled noodles with meat and vegetables.
Monty, steamed dumplings, shashlic, grilled meat on sticks,
samsa baked pastries with meat or pumpkin.
What do people drink in Uzbekistan?
People drink tea, green or black, often without sugar.
Compote, sweet fruit drink, iron, salty yogurt drink.
In summer, adults may drink local wine or vodka, but it is not common.
Tea is served in small bowls, not cups.
What is life like in Uzbekistan?
Life in Uzbekistan is friendly, traditional and family-based.
People enjoy spending time with family and neighbors, eating meals together, walking in parks and bazaars,
listening to music and dancing, visiting mosques and historic places.
In villages, people grow fruit, cotton or vegetables.
What are some holidays and traditions in Uzbekistan?
Navru's Spring Festival on March 21st with music, food and games.
Independence Day, September 1st.
Eid al-Feder and Eid al-Ada islamic holidays, Constitution Day, December 8th.
Weddings, big events with food, music and dance.
People wear traditional clothes and hospitality is very important.
Some fun facts about Uzbekistan.
Uzbekistan is one of only two double landlocked countries in the world.
Samarkand, Bukhara and Kiva are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The flag is blue, white and green with a crescent, moon and stars.
Uzbek hospitality is famous, guests are always welcome.
Most houses have a teapot ready for visitors.
Now you know many things about Uzbekistan.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the cities, food and traditions.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Uzbek, shite.
